title: Hibernate or migrate: how animals survive winter
examples: What happens to an animal's body in hibernation?
Why do some animals migrate and others hibernate?

explain.say: Winter brings cold and little food. Some animals stay and switch their bodies into an energy-saving mode called hibernation, while others travel to where food is, which is migration.

draw.text: Hibernate or migrate: how animals survive winter

explain.say: A hibernating animal, such as a hedgehog, dormouse or ground squirrel, lets its body cool to near the temperature of its burrow. Its breathing and heartbeat slow right down, so its stored fat lasts all winter.

A woodchuck's heart beats about 80 times a minute in summer but only about 5 times a minute in hibernation. Hibernators still wake up briefly every week or two, warming up again, before sinking back down.

Migrating is the other strategy: swallows fly to Africa, where insects are plentiful, and caribou trek to better feeding grounds. It costs energy and risk, but the animal stays active and keeps eating.

faq.q: What happens to an animal's body in hibernation?
faq.a: Its body temperature drops, sometimes to just a few degrees above freezing, and its heartbeat, breathing and use of energy slow enormously. It lives off fat stored in autumn.
Yes, though differently from small hibernators. A bear's temperature falls only a few degrees, but it can go months without eating, drinking or passing waste, and mothers even give birth in the den.
asks: Is a bear's winter sleep hibernation?
Do bears wake up in winter?

faq.q: Why do hibernating animals wake up during winter?
faq.a: Most small hibernators warm up briefly every week or two. Nobody is completely sure why; it may help their immune system or let them truly sleep, but these wake-ups use most of their winter energy.
asks: Why do hedgehogs wake in winter?

faq.q: Why do some animals migrate and others hibernate?
faq.a: It depends on body and lifestyle. Birds and big mammals can travel far to find food, while small animals that cannot travel far, like dormice and bats, save energy by hibernating instead.

faq.q: How do animals get ready for hibernation?
faq.a: In autumn they eat extra food and build up fat, sometimes gaining a large share of their body weight. Some, like chipmunks, also store food, and they find a sheltered den, burrow or hollow.
asks: What do animals do before hibernating?
Why do animals get fat in autumn?

facts: Arctic ground squirrels can let their body temperature fall to about minus 3 °C during hibernation (Barnes, 1989).
A woodchuck's heart rate drops from about 80 to about 5 beats a minute in hibernation.
